title: Locating the corrupted byte inside a Flate stream
statement: Scattered byte substitutions inside a DEFLATE stream rarely make the decoder fail where the damage is: most damaged streams decode to the end and fail only the Adler-32 check, and when zlib does fail it is thousands of compressed bytes later. Brown's recovery needs the corrupt region as input and detects it automatically only for runs of at least 128 identical bytes; two general-case detectors failed. Localisation is the prerequisite for a trustworthy salvaged prefix (grade 2), for intra-block resynchronization, and for bounding any correction search. Candidate signals for PDF: content-stream operator grammar and operand plausibility, font-table structure (TrueType table directory/checksums), /Length1 of font files, decoded-length consistency, and per-position Adler-32 constraints.
inference: The PDF-specific localisation signals listed are our proposal; the literature evaluated localisation only on natural-language text.
still_open_evidence: OpenCitations v2 (2026-09-27): the 6 works citing Brown 2013 (Force Open, two database-carving papers, DVR fragments, OOXML syntactic reconstruction, pugz) and the 4 citing Barral 2022 do not address automatic corruption localisation in DEFLATE; Barral 2022 avoids localisation by brute force over all positions.

title: Salvaged prefixes contain silently wrong bytes
statement: 'Decode until the decoder errors' is the usual salvage for a damaged Flate stream and is what the charter's provenance grade 2 ('salvaged prefix of a corrupt stream') suggests. On REPDF C9 this emits wrong bytes in 95% of damaged streams (median 11,426 per stream), because the error surfaces late or only at the Adler-32 check. No DEFLATE-recovery work measures or bounds these bytes; Brown measures reconstruction precision but assumes the corrupt region is known. Needed: a salvage policy that certifies how much of the emitted prefix is verbatim (e.g. cut at a localised corruption point, or cut conservatively and label the rest), and a fabrication metric that counts these bytes.
inference: That grade-2 output is currently unsafe is our reading of OBS-0300 against charter s2; the literature does not state it for prefix salvage.
still_open_evidence: No screened or citing work (OpenCitations forward snowball of Brown 2011/2013, Park 2008, Barral 2022) reports the number of wrongly emitted bytes of prefix salvage.

title: Intra-block resynchronization for single-block PDF streams
statement: Published DEFLATE resynchronization mostly restarts at the next intact block (Brown 2011, pugz, gzrt, Adler's salvage), and pugz confirms a block start only when five more blocks decode. In REPDF, 64% of Flate streams are a single block and 68% of damaged C9 streams have no block after the damage, so block-level resync recovers nothing there. Brown 2013's intra-block method (all candidate restart offsets converge within at most 150 bytes, given the block's Huffman tables) fits this case but was evaluated only on text ZIPs with one known zeroed region. Untested: intra-block resync on PDF content, font and image streams, combined with automatic localisation, with the unknown history carried as co-indexed symbols.
inference: Transfer to PDF is our inference; Brown's convergence result comes from natural-language text.
still_open_evidence: OpenCitations v2 citing works of Brown 2013 (6) and pugz (11: bioinformatics I/O, FPGA, rapidgzip, truncated-gzip recovery) include no application of intra-block resync to PDF or other document streams; rapidgzip and Luo 2024 were screened by title/abstract only.

title: Content models to reconstruct unknown bytes in non-prose PDF streams
statement: Unknown-byte reconstruction after lost history (co-indexed unknowns) exists only for natural-language text: Brown's models need word-like units, repetitive markup tags are the hardest case, and pugz left guessing undetermined characters unexplored. PDF streams are mostly not prose: content-stream operators (repetitive, markup-like), CMaps, font programs, XMP. Needed: format-aware models (operator grammar, font-table structure, per-producer n-grams) and measurement of recall and precision of reconstructed bytes, with every reconstructed byte labelled as inferred (grade 4) rather than recovered.
inference: That PDF streams resemble markup more than prose is our inference, as is the proposed labelling of reconstructed bytes as grade 4.
still_open_evidence: No work citing Brown 2011/2013 or pugz (OpenCitations v2) builds non-text reconstruction models; ML file-repair works screened (audio, H.264 video) repair decoded signals, not compressed-stream bytes.

title: Checksum-guided Flate correction: ambiguity and PDF-level tie-breakers
statement: Barral et al. repair zlib data by brute-forcing one or two bit flips with Adler-32 as the only oracle: 172 of 204 fragments get a unique candidate, but 3 get several even under one flip, double flips yield up to 40,717 valid candidates and months of computation, and ties are broken by hand or left as indeterminate bits. Adler-32 is weak on short inputs, and many PDF streams are short. In REPDF C9 each damaged Flate stream has exactly one substituted byte (a 255-value byte substitution, not a bit flip), which makes the per-stream search bounded, but the charter's grade 3 ('Adler-32 match') is not sufficient for uniqueness. Open: the false-correction rate for byte substitutions in PDF streams, and PDF-specific secondary oracles (decoded length vs /Length1 or /DL, TrueType table checksums, content-stream grammar, cross-stream consistency) that turn ambiguous candidates into unique ones or into explicit indeterminate spans.
inference: The secondary oracles are our proposal; that one byte per damaged stream bounds the search is our reading of OBS-0300. It also qualifies the charter's constraint flag: per file C9 changes 12-30 bytes (OBS-0002), but per damaged Flate stream it is one byte.
still_open_evidence: Barral 2022 is the only checksum-guided DEFLATE correction found; its 4 citing works (OpenCitations v2, 2026-09-27) are surveys or device forensics that do not extend the method. Not read: Wang/Zhao/Sun 2018 and Wang/Peng/Tang 2019 (LZSS/Huffman fault tolerance), which may contain related search methods.

title: Per-instance repair-strategy selection trained on correctness, with abstention
statement: RQ5 (gentle-gosling s2) asks how to map diagnostic findings to a repair toolpath. The closest evidence is algorithm selection applied to program repair (E-APR): effectiveness is instance-dependent, no technique is best everywhere, and a selector picks a technique with 88% precision. But it is trained on plausible repairs (tests pass), because correctness labels were too scarce, and it has no reject option. For PDF the analogue of 'plausible' is 'opens in a viewer', which is exactly what hides fabrication. No work applies per-instance selection to file or document repair. Needed: diagnostic features per file or stream (damage signature, blocks per stream, checksum status, candidate count), labels from fidelity against known originals rather than 'opens', evaluation against single-best and oracle (virtual-best) toolpaths, and an abstention threshold that routes low-confidence cases to NeedsInteraction.
inference: The PDF feature set, the 'opens-in-viewer = plausible' analogy and the abstention design are ours. Chow's reject rule, learning-to-defer and guided data repair (screened, not read) are the candidate methods for the threshold and escalation parts.
still_open_evidence: OpenCitations v2 (2026-09-27): the 12 works citing E-APR are program-repair, SBSE or instance-space papers; none applies selection to file/document repair. A paid search for strategy selection in corrupted-file repair returned nothing relevant (SRCH-0307).

title: No benchmark for compressed-stream recovery in documents
statement: DEFLATE-recovery evaluations use damage their methods are built to detect (a zeroed contiguous run at a fixed offset) on plain-text ZIPs, and report reconstruction recall and precision only for the region downstream of a known corruption. Real and benchmark damage differ: REPDF C9 is one substituted byte per stream, and real flash damage is sparse bit flips. There is no shared corpus of damaged PDF (or any document) Flate streams with ground truth and metrics covering detection, verbatim bytes, silently wrong bytes, reconstructed-byte precision and ambiguity. Needed: a stream-level benchmark carved from known-original PDFs with several damage models (bit flips at a measured rate, byte substitutions, zero-filled sectors, lost stream start, truncation) and those metrics.
inference: The claim that evaluation damage matches the detector is our reading of CLM-0308 and CLM-0313 together.
still_open_evidence: Grajeda et al. 2017 (dataset survey, title-screened only) and the Parallel search SRCH-0306 found no compressed-stream recovery benchmark; the only corrupted-bitstream benchmark found (BSCV, NeurIPS 2023) is H.264 video.
